Eweka I.fact: Egharevba credits him with creating the state councillors or kingmakers later called the Uzama Nihinron and lists Oliha, Edohen, Ezomo, Ero, Eholo n'Ire and Oloton as the original members.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: He states that Eweka made the offices hereditary and directed that future Obas be crowned by Oliha because the group had been responsible for the appeal to Ife that resulted in _____'s arrival
Eweka I.fact: He states that Eweka made the offices hereditary and directed that future Obas be crowned by Oliha because the group had been responsible for the appeal to Ife that resulted in Oranmiyan's arrival.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: Egharevba further states that the later _____ added the Edaiken, or crown prince, increasing the group to seven members
Eweka I.fact: Egharevba further states that the later Oba Ewuare added the Edaiken, or crown prince, increasing the group to seven members.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: Irabor characterises Eweka's relationship with the _____ as one of divided authority and describes the early Oba as a primus inter pares, or first among equals, rather than as a dominant monarch
Eweka I.fact: Osadolor gives a different institutional history, stating that an older council called the Edionnisen was expanded to six members through the addition of Oloton, an adviser and guardian of Eweka who had arrived from Ife, and that the body later became called the Uzama. Irabor characterises Eweka's relationship with the Uzama as one of divided authority and describes the early Oba as a primus inter pares, or first among equals, rather than as a dominant monarch.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: In his reconstruction, _____ and his followers retained effective power in the Benin capital while Eweka and the following two Obas remained at Usama with the Uzama
Eweka I.fact: In his reconstruction, Ogiamien and his followers retained effective power in the Benin capital while Eweka and the following two Obas remained at Usama with the Uzama.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: He further states that much of the population along the _____ did not recognise the authority of the Oba during this early phase
Eweka I.fact: He further states that much of the population along the Ikpoba River did not recognise the authority of the Oba during this early phase.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: More extensive royal control over the capital and nearby territory is placed under Ewedo, the fourth Oba, following his defeat of the rival faction at _____
Eweka I.fact: More extensive royal control over the capital and nearby territory is placed under Ewedo, the fourth Oba, following his defeat of the rival faction at Ekiokpagha.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: Egharevba states that disputes among Eweka's many children led him to send some away as _____, or chiefs, of separate villages
Eweka I.fact: Egharevba states that disputes among Eweka's many children led him to send some away as Enigie, or chiefs, of separate villages. Irabor similarly writes that Eweka installed sons as Enigie and made them rulers of outlying Benin communities.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: He also preserves a tradition accusing _____ of having "polluted" his father's bed
Eweka I.fact: He also preserves a tradition accusing Omonuza of having "polluted" his father's bed. Elsewhere, Egharevba identifies Omorodion, commonly called Odion at Uwokha, as one of Eweka's older sons and ranks him immediately after Omonuza in seniority.

Eweka I.fact: Uwakhuahen, one of Eweka's older sons, succeeded him and was in turn followed by his brother Ehenmihen. Eweka I.question: Osadolor records a different succession narrative in which _____ was Eweka's eldest son but was excluded from the throne by the Uzama, who supported the younger Uwakhuahen
Eweka I.fact: Osadolor records a different succession narrative in which Prince Idu was Eweka's eldest son but was excluded from the throne by the Uzama, who supported the younger Uwakhuahen.

Osadolor records a different succession narrative in which Prince Idu was Eweka's eldest son but was excluded from the throne by the Uzama, who supported the younger Uwakhuahen.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: Idu threatened war and gained support from his mother's community and elders in _____, after which the southeastern section of the kingdom was ceded to him and became the kingdom of Ugu
Eweka I.fact: Idu threatened war and gained support from his mother's community and elders in Iyekorhionmwon, after which the southeastern section of the kingdom was ceded to him and became the kingdom of Ugu.

Eweka I.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Eweka I.question: Egharevba preserves a separate post-succession narrative concerning _____
Eweka I.fact: Egharevba preserves a separate post-succession narrative concerning Omorodion. He states that Omorodion was passed over for the throne after Eweka died and subsequently left the Benin capital with his family and followers to found Uwokha in Ivbiosakon.

Eweka I.fact: According to the tradition, the instruction was carried out, and thereafter the remains of a Benin Oba were taken to Ife every third reign.
